question_en: Which of the following orders is said to be "behind the market"?
option_a: Market sell order when the best bid is 38 and the best ask is 39.
option_b: Limit sell order at 38 when the best ask is 39.
option_c: Limit buy order at 38 when the best bid is 39.
explanation_en: A limit buy order is behind the market if its limit price is below the best bid. A limit sell order is behind the market if its limit price is above the best ask. Market orders are never said to be behind the market.

question_en: Which of the following statements about the maintenance margin requirement is least accurate?
option_a: The Federal Reserve sets the maximum maintenance margin.
option_b: The purpose of the maintenance margin requirement is to protect the broker in the event of a large stock decline.
option_c: Generally the maintenance margin requirement is lower than the initial margin requirement.
explanation_en: The Federal Reserve sets the minimum maintenance margin and individual investment companies may set higher margins if they wish.

question_en: Mark Ritchie purchased, on margin, 200 shares of TMX Corp. stock at a price of $35 per share. The margin requirement was 50%. The stock price has increased to $42 per share. What is Ritchie's return on investment before commissions and interest if he decides to sell his TMX holdings now?
explanation_en: 200 shares × $35 = $7000 Initial Market Value $7000 × .50 = $3500 cash payment and $3500 borrowed. The new market value of the stock after price increase is (200 × $42) = $8400. If Ritchie sold his holdings he would have $4900 ($8400 – $3500) left after the loan was paid. So Ritchie's return on his original $3500 investment is: $4900/3500 – 1 = 1.4 – 1.0 = 0.40 = 40%.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 41 Market Organization and Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following conditions is most likely necessary for capital to be allocated to its most valuable uses?
option_a: Financial markets are frictionless (i.e., free of taxes or transactions costs).
option_b: Investors are well informed about the risk and return of various investments.
option_c: There are no barriers to the flow of complete information to the financial markets.
explanation_en: Capital will flow to its most valuable uses if markets function well and investors are well informed about the risk and return characteristics of various investments. Allocation of capital to its most valuable uses does not require that all investors have complete information or that financial markets are frictionless.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 41 Market Organization and Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: An objective of financial market regulation is to:
option_a: ensure that inside information is made public in a timely manner.
option_b: prevent uninformed investors from participating in financial markets.
option_c: reduce information gathering costs by requiring common financial reporting standards.
explanation_en: One of the objectives of market regulation is to require firms to report their financial performance according to a single set of standards, such as those of the IASB or FASB, thereby reducing market participants' cost of gathering information. Market regulation is not designed to prevent uninformed investors from trading, but to protect unsophisticated investors and thereby preserve trust in the financial markets. An objective of market regulation is to prevent those with non-public information from profiting at the expense of other investors, but not necessarily to make all inside information public.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 41 Market Organization and Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: An investor bought a stock on margin. The margin requirement was 60%, the current price of the stock is $80, and the stock price was $50 one year ago. If margin interest is 5%, how much equity did the investor have in the investment at year-end?
explanation_en: Margin debt = 40% × $50 = $20; Interest = $20 × 0.05 = $1. Equity % = [Value – (margin debt + interest)] / Value $80 - $21 / $80 = 73.8%

question_en: Toby Jensen originally purchased 400 shares of CSC stock on margin at a price of $60 per share. The initial margin requirement is 50% and the maintenance margin is 25%. CSC stock price has fallen dramatically in recent months and it closed today with a sharp decline bringing the closing price to $40 per share. Will Jensen receive a margin call?
option_a: No, he meets the minimum initial margin requirement.
option_b: No, he meets the minimum maintenance margin requirement.
option_c: Yes, he does not meet the minimum maintenance margin requirement.
explanation_en: Total original value held by Jensen is 400 × $60 = $24,000. Amount of equity is 50% ($24,000) = $12,000. Current total value is 400 × $40 = $16,000. So Jensen's equity is $16,000 - $12,000 = $4,000 which is 4,000/16,000 = 25% of the total market value.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 41 Market Organization and Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A trader enters a limit order to buy 10,000 shares as a day order. The "day order" instruction is most accurately referred to as:
explanation_en: Validity instructions specify when a trade is to be executed. Specification of a day order (as opposed to a good-til-canceled order) is a validity instruction.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 41 Market Organization and Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following statements about securities exchanges is most accurate?
option_a: Call markets are markets in which the stock is only traded at specific times.
option_b: Continuous markets are markets where trades occur 24 hours per day.
option_c: Setting a negotiated price to clear the market is a method used to set the closing price in major continuous markets.
explanation_en: Continuous markets are markets where trades occur at any time the market is open (i.e., they do not need to be open 24 hours per day). Setting one negotiated price is a method used in major continuous markets to set the opening price.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 41 Market Organization and Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following statements about financial intermediaries is most accurate?
option_a: Arbitrageurs buy securities with the anticipation that they will be able to sell the securities in the future at higher prices.
option_b: Brokers seek out traders that are willing to take the opposite sides of their clients’ orders.
option_c: Dealers buy a security in one market and simultaneously sell the same security in a different market.
explanation_en: Brokers seek out traders that are willing to take the opposite side of their clients' orders. Arbitrageurs buy an instrument in one market and simultaneously sell the same instrument in a different market at a higher price. Dealers buy securities from clients, with the expectation that they will be able to sell the securities to other clients in the future at higher prices.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 41 Market Organization and Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following statements regarding primary and secondary markets is least accurate?
option_a: New issues of government securities can be sold on the primary market.
option_b: Prevailing market prices are determined by primary market transactions and are used in pricing new issues.
option_c: Secondary market transactions occur between two investors and do not involve the firm that originally issued the security.
explanation_en: Prevailing market prices are determined by the transactions that take place on the secondary market. This information is used to determine the price of new issues sold on primary markets.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 41 Market Organization and Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: A financial system in which transactions have low costs is said to exhibit:
explanation_en: Operational efficiency refers to low transactions costs. A financial system exhibits informational efficiency if prices quickly reflect all information relevant to fundamental value. A market exhibits allocational efficiency if it results in capital being directed to its most productive uses.

question_en: A buy limit order is said to be "inside the market" when:
option_a: the limit is between the best bid and the best ask.
option_c: the order is entered in the limit book.
explanation_en: A limit order with a limit price between the best bid and the best ask is said to be "inside the market" or "making a new market." A limit order that has not yet been executed is a "standing limit order."

question_en: Becky Kirk contacted her broker and placed an order to purchase 1,000 shares of Bricko Corp. stock at a price of $60 per share. Kirk wishes to buy on margin. Assuming the margin requirement is 40%, how much money does Kirk have to pay up front to make the purchase?
explanation_en: The margin requirement represents the amount of money an investor must put down on the purchase. So Kirk must put $24,000 down ($60,000 × .40 = $24,000) and can borrow the balance.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 41 Market Organization and Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Austin Bruno, CFA, places a fill or kill, limit buy order at 92 for a stock. Bruno's order specifies:
explanation_en: Fill or kill is a validity instruction as it indicates when the order can be filled (i.e. immediately or cancel the order). A limit buy order is an execution instruction as it indicates how the order should be filled (e.g. buy at $92 or less). Clearing instructions indicate how to settle the trade (i.e., how and when to transfer the cash and the security).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Equity Investments\Reading 41 Market Organization and Structure - Answers.pdf
question_en: Byron Campbell purchased 300 shares of Crescent, Inc., stock at a price of $80 per share. The purchase was made on margin with an initial margin requirement of 50%. Assuming the maintenance margin is 25%, the stock price of Crescent, Inc. has to fall below what level for Campbell to receive a margin call?
explanation_en: Trigger price (margin purchases) = Po (1 – initial margin) / (1 – maintenance margin). $80(1 - .5) / (1 - .25) = 40 / .75 = $53.33. P = $53.33 If Crescent, Inc. falls below $53.33 then Campbell will get a margin call.

question_en: A trader pays $100 per share to buy 500 shares of a non-dividend-paying firm. The purchase is done on margin, and the leverage ratio at purchase is 3.0X. Three months later, the trader sells the shares for $90 per share. Ignoring transaction costs and interest paid on the margin loan, the trader's 3-month return was closest to:
explanation_en: With a leverage ratio of 3 and a 10% decrease in share value, the investor's return is 3 × – 10% = –30%.
